html:
The Khazar Khaganate was a state of the semi-nomadic Turkic Khazars that ruled the lands between the Volga, the Don, the north Caucasus and Crimea from about 650 until the 960s. It controlled the trade routes between the Caspian and the Black Sea.

The Khazars rose out of the break-up of the western Türk Khaganate. Their state was multilingual and held many peoples: Turks, Slavs, Alans, Jews, Christians, Muslims and pagans.

Why they mattered:

  • They fought the Arabs of the Umayyad Caliphate in the Caucasus for decades in the 7th and 8th centuries and kept Islam south of the mountains.
  • They were allies of the Byzantine Empire. An emperor married a Khazar princess.
  • Their capital Atil on the lower Volga was a hub for furs, slaves, silver and silk between Scandinavia, Baghdad and China.
  • Their ruling class adopted Judaism, probably in the 8th or 9th century. How far the conversion reached among ordinary people is unknown.

The rise of Kievan Rus' ended them. Around 965 the Rus' prince Sviatoslav I destroyed the Khazar fortress of Sarkel, and Atil fell in the following years. Pechenegs and later Cumans took over the steppe as part of the wider Turkic migrations.

Little Khazar writing survives, so most of what we know comes from Arab, Byzantine, Hebrew and Rus' sources.
